PullRequest.Title: Make focus visible on checked toggle buttons
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #190382 Checked toggle buttons previously kept their active border while focused, making keyboard focus hard to distinguish. This change stores the active border color in a CSS variable and replaces it with the standard dashed focus border for `:focus-visible`, while pointer focus keeps the existing checked appearance. A themed component fixture covers the checked keyboard-focus state in light, dark, and high-contrast themes. ## Before / After
Before After
## Validation - `npm run eslint -- src/vs/base/browser/ui/toggle/toggle.ts src/vs/workbench/test/browser/componentFixtures/baseUI.fixture.ts` - `npm run stylelint -- src/vs/base/browser/ui/toggle/toggle.css` - Verified keyboard and pointer focus states in light, dark, High Contrast, and High Contrast Light

Scenarios.Scenario: Constructing and checking/unchecking Toggle controls in Search, Find, notebook, settings, and toolbar UI
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Toggle construction and each checked-state assignment synchronously update ARIA/class state and three inline styles. The diff replaces one direct border-color write with one custom-property set/remove; no geometry read, collection traversal, async wait, or expensive boundary blocks the interaction.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of Toggle instances constructed or explicitly updated. Cost remains O(1) per Toggle and is not moved into a frame, scroll, or large-list loop by the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous on the UI thread for the single Toggle receiving the state change. Callers generally own a small fixed set of controls (for example, three related Search toggles), and the diff adds no queue, fan-out, or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates. The stylesheet is already loaded with the component, and each changed Toggle recomputes only its own style state; cold construction and warm state changes have the same bounded custom-property mutation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the constructor and checked setter both call applyStyles, and the changed branch performs exactly one setProperty or removeProperty on that Toggle's DOM node.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser custom-property invalidation cost varies by engine/theme, but the affected element has no DOM subtree beyond its icon pseudo-element and realistic cardinality is a handful of toggles, so there is no credible user-visible regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changed style mutation is equivalent in count and scope to the previous inline borderColor assignment and does not amplify synchronous UI work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Keyboard or pointer focus moving onto a Toggle
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Browser focus selector matching and border repaint occur before the focused state is visible. The new :focus and :focus-visible rules match the focused Toggle only and perform no JavaScript or forced layout.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Focus transitions, not workspace size or result count. Each transition affects at most the newly focused and previously focused elements.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One active focused element at a time in a document; focus transitions are serialized by the browser event loop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Normal browser stylesheet matching applies; there is no application cache or miss path. The shared CSS rule is loaded once and reused across all Toggle instances.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed CSS consists only of a simple class/:not/:focus selector and a border declaration on the focused node.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact style/repaint duration is browser-dependent, but selector scope is one focused element and no layout read/write feedback loop exists.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new focus paint is bounded and is the intended visible behavior, with no synchronous layout mechanism or repeated subtree work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Component-fixture CI renders the new checked keyboard-focus state in Dark, Light, Dark High Contrast, and Light High Contrast
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For each theme variant, the existing fixture harness synchronously creates one Toggle, appends it, and focuses it before the existing screenshot pipeline can capture and compare the result. Screenshot generation is on the CI fixture critical path but not any product runtime path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Render and capture one screenshot artifact for each screenshot-labeled theme variant
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four new bounded captures: Dark, Light, DarkHighContrast, and LightHighContrast; no per-item product collection or retry loop is introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The KeyboardFocusedToggle fixture did not exist, so this workflow produced zero captures for this state; the screenshot infrastructure itself is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds four expected captures to the visual-regression CI workflow; it is entirely off the product interaction/startup critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse the rendered manifest and committed screenshot markdown, then compare generated markdown
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two existing file reads per comparator invocation, unchanged by the diff; the manifest gains four bounded entries and the markdown gains four bounded image records.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same two files were read once; only four small records were absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs only in the existing CI comparison step after fixture rendering; the diff does not add filesystem calls or move them onto a product path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed four theme variants, each with one DOM node; this does not scale with workspace, files, search results, history, or user lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The diff defines four independent variants (two default themes plus two additional themes) and adds no local Promise.all, limiter, queue, or subprocess scheduling. Actual cross-fixture parallelism remains owned by the unchanged external fixture runner; within each render there is one Toggle and one focus call.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each theme variant is a separate fixture render; no cache or coalescing is shown between variants. The fixed cardinality of four is explicit, and screenshot hashes are committed as static markdown references.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the four added variants and one Toggle per variant; medium for screenshot runtime details because capture scheduling belongs to unchanged external infrastructure.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The external runner's exact screenshot duration and cross-fixture concurrency are not visible in the changed code, but the added cardinality is exactly four and each fixture contains one tiny component.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The bounded CI cost is intentional coverage, while generated allowlist/markdown additions add only constant-size metadata.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all five changed files and all diff pages. Traced Toggle construction/state updates, browser focus rendering, representative Search/Find callers, ownership/disposal, and the four-theme component-fixture path including its existing filesystem comparison. No diff-introduced hot-path, scaling, retention, cache-lifecycle, concurrency, or expensive-boundary regression met the reporting threshold.
